blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Taxes can sound hard, but in English they follow simple patterns. Every country has its own tax system. Brazil has one system, while the UK has a different one.

The Brazilian system has many rules. It is complex, so the team checks every form. The UK system is more simple, but it still has clear rules. We must read both with care.

Sophie helps the fiscal team. She explains the tax words slowly, in simple English. One step at a time, taxes become easy. You can do it!

items.q: How many tax systems does the text talk about?
items.why: "Brazil has one system, while the UK has a different one." — dois países, dois sistemas.

items.q: What does the text say about the Brazilian system?
options: It has many rules and is complex
It is the same as the UK system
items.why: "The Brazilian system has many rules. It is complex."

items.q: Who explains the tax words to the team?
items.why: "Sophie helps the fiscal team. She explains the tax words slowly."

items.q: The text suggests that the UK system, compared to Brazil, is…
items.why: Inferência: "more simple, but it still has clear rules" — mais fácil, porém ainda com regras.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: with small steps, taxes become easy
you should never ask for help
English tax words are always hard
items.why: Inferência: "One step at a time, taxes become easy. You can do it!" — o tom é encorajador.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicar como o time trabalha com os impostos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, I'm Sophie. Let me show you how we work with taxes here. It is not so hard when you go step by step.

Every month, we check the tax forms for two countries. Brazil is one country, and the UK is the other. The two systems are not the same. The Brazilian system has many rules, so it takes more time. The UK system is more simple, but we still read every line.

First, I open the form on my computer. Then I check the numbers. If one number is wrong, I fix it before we send the form. We never send a form with a mistake.

Some rules are complex, so I read them slowly. When I don't understand a rule, I ask my manager. It is better to ask than to guess.

We also watch the tax calendar. There is a deadline every month, and the form must be ready on time.

Don't worry if it feels hard at the start. Taxes become easy with practice. One small step at a time, and soon you will do it alone. You can do it!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many countries does Sophie check the forms for?
items.why: "we check the tax forms for two countries. Brazil is one country, and the UK is the other."

items.q: What does Sophie do if one number is wrong?
options: She fixes it before sending the form
She asks the client to fix it
items.why: "If one number is wrong, I fix it before we send the form."

items.q: What does Sophie do when she doesn't understand a rule?
items.why: "When I don't understand a rule, I ask my manager. It is better to ask than to guess."

items.q: Sophie says the Brazilian system "takes more time." This suggests that…
options: the UK system is faster to check
the UK system takes more time
items.why: Inferência: se o brasileiro é mais complexo e demora mais, o britânico ("more simple") é mais rápido.

items.q: How does Sophie want the new person to feel?
options: Calm and confident, one step at a time
items.why: Inferência: "Don't worry… One small step at a time… You can do it!" — ela passa calma e confiança.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We open the tax system on the computer every morning." A system is…
options: a set of parts that work together
items.why: System = sistema: um conjunto de partes que funcionam juntas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "There is a new tax ___ this month, so we must read it before we send the form."
items.why: Rule = regra: a nova regra fiscal do mês.

items.q: "Brazil is one country, and the UK is another." A country is…
options: a nation with its own laws
items.why: Country = país: uma nação com suas próprias leis.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "This rule is very ___, so Sophie reads it slowly."
items.why: Complex = complexo: difícil, com muitas partes.

items.q: "The UK form is simple, so it takes only a few minutes." Simple means…
items.why: Simple = simples: fácil, sem complicação.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem no trabalho com formulários e impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Please fill in the tax form with your numbers." To fill in means to…
options: write the information in the blank spaces
items.why: Fill in = preencher: escrever as informações nos espaços em branco.

items.q: "We must hand in the form before the deadline." To hand in means to…
options: give or send it to the right person
items.why: Hand in = entregar: dar/enviar para quem deve receber.

items.q: "Can you check over the numbers before we send them?" To check over means to…
options: look at it carefully to find mistakes
items.why: Check over = revisar: olhar com cuidado para achar erros.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar oficialmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "I need to find out the new tax rule for this month." To find out means to…
items.why: Find out = descobrir: aprender/obter uma informação que você não tinha.
